With all the fuckery of our current systems, it's still difficult to come up with something more important and crucial than our right to vote, and we don't even know how many fucking COINFLIPS happened? This is a shitshow.

I don't have a problem with coinflips as a concept. When you have <200 people evenly split, A coinflip sounds good to me. I would say that reporting it as a tie and splitting the delegate would be better, but coinflips still in theory work just as well.

The problem is with reporting, and that is just a problem of caucuses as a concept. But I don't know if that is something that should change:

  • Primaries are more expensive than a caucus. To do an effective primary, they need a long paper trail, more volunteers for counting.
  • Caucuses are way more fun and exciting than a secret ballot.
  • Primaries are more opaque and don't inspire confidence in the voting system. A caucus lets people see very visually how many people are voting for what, and avoids local questions of ballot stuffing (local politics is where that happens, nationally it gets more creative than just ballot stuffing). A secret ballot does not inspire confidence in people that there isn't a larger conspiracy going on, since they can't count everyone's vote themselves.
  • This is just for a political party, and has nothing to do with the government. If we had the laikaislost_for_supreme_dictator party, I would think that the election for that party's representative should be chosen how that party sees fit. So, for example, the laikaislost_for_supreme_dictator party should nominate by asking laikaislost, and ignoring everyone else's opinion. Then people can vote for that candidate or someone else as defined in the constitution during the actual election.
